original_question: Let mu be a probability measure on a bounded pseudoconvex domain Omega in C^n. Assume there exists a Holder continuous plurisubharmonic subsolution u on Omega with u|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu <= (dd^c u)^n. Determine whether there must exist a Holder continuous plurisubharmonic function phi on Omega with phi|_{partial Omega} = 0 and mu = (dd^c phi)^n.
target_in_paper: Section 2.4, Question 17 (Zeriahi): the local Hölder subsolution problem for the zero-boundary Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge–Ampère equation on a bounded pseudoconvex domain Ω ⊂ ℂ^n. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s target almost verbatim: it has the correct ambient setting (a bounded pseudoconvex domain Ω ⊂ ℂ^n), the correct datum (a probability measure μ), the right hypothesis (existence of a Hölder continuous plurisubharmonic subsolution u with u|∂Ω = 0 and μ ≤ (dd^c u)^n in Ω), and the exact sought conclusion (existence of a Hölder continuous plurisubharmonic φ with φ|∂Ω = 0 and μ = (dd^c φ)^n in Ω). ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
missing_details: The paper formulates this as an open problem, specifically Question 17 (Zeriahi), not as a theorem or conjecture; that status should be made explicit in a paper-faithful rewrite. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The nearby context matters: immediately before Question 17, the authors explain that [D&all14] solves the analogous global compact Hölder subsolution problem, and that the unresolved issue is precisely the local version. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

For a fully stand-alone statement, it is better to spell out that u, φ ∈ PSH(Ω) and that (dd^c·)^n denotes the local complex Monge–Ampère measure; the inequality and equality are to hold in Ω. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

To make the boundary condition mathematically explicit, the refined question should say that the Hölder continuous psh functions have zero boundary values in the Dirichlet sense (equivalently, one usually reads this as Hölder continuity up to ∂Ω). The paper uses the boundary condition explicitly but leaves that regularity-on-closure wording implicit. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The paper does not prescribe a specific Hölder exponent α, so the refined question should not add one unless explicitly intended; it asks only for some Hölder continuous subsolution and some Hölder continuous solution. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
refined_question: Question 17 (local Hölder subsolution problem). Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain, and let μ be a probability measure on Ω. Suppose there exists a Hölder continuous plurisubharmonic function u ∈ PSH(Ω), with zero boundary values u|∂Ω = 0, such that μ ≤ (dd^c u)^n in Ω, where (dd^c·)^n denotes the local complex Monge–Ampère measure. Must there exist a Hölder continuous plurisubharmonic function φ ∈ PSH(Ω), also with φ|∂Ω = 0, such that μ = (dd^c φ)^n in Ω?
justification: The draft is essentially a direct paraphrase of Question 17 (Zeriahi). The closest official formulation is therefore the question itself, not a broader range-of-the-operator problem. The sentence immediately preceding Question 17 explains the intended scope: [D&all14] gives a technical characterization of MA(Hol(X, ω)) and solves the analogous global Hölder subsolution problem, so the authors isolate the unresolved local Hölder subsolution problem. The neighboring Question 14 is the continuous analogue, confirming that your draft is targeting the Hölder upgrade of that same Dirichlet-subsolution question rather than a different problem. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
